title: Full Roos realization of completed integral pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. Write $L^0_W=\lim\circ U_W$ and $r_W=\operatorname{leftAdjoint}(L^0_W)$ for ordinary coherent reduction, equipped with its specified adjunction $r_W\dashv L^0_W$ and unit $\eta^0_W$; concretely its components are quotient extension $B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}M$ and its transitions are induced by the actual quotient maps. A superscript $c$ means termwise application to cochain complexes. For a coherent complex $C$, let $\lambda_C:q_W((L^0_W)^c C)\to\mathcal L_W(q^s_WC)$ be the canonical right-derived limit unit, with the exact-restriction/localization factorization inserted (the map named pullbackTensorLimitUnit). For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$, let $b_f$ on sequence sites be $(n,V)\mapsto(n,X\times_Y V)$. Its ring map is the actual constant-section coefficient map at every $n$; let $f^s_*:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_Y$ be its module direct image, $F_f:\mathscr S_Y\to\mathscr S_X$ its specified left adjoint, $\eta^f$ the unit, and $D_f=D(F_f)$ the exact induced derived inverse image [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Finite module pullback $f_n^*$ is equipped with its actual adjunction unit. The direct-image/evaluation comparison is identity on sections; the fixed inverse-image/evaluation isomorphism $v_{f,n}:f_n^* e_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{X,n}F_f$ is its inverse mate under the specified finite and sequence adjunctions. For a complex $T$ of strict $A_W$-module towers, let $J_W(T)$ denote reordering to a tower of complexes, and put $H_W(T)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nJ_W(T)_n\to\prod_nJ_W(T)_n)[-1]$, where $s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$ uses the actual transitions [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. Write $H_W$ also for the resulting cochain functor. The map $j_I:(\lim)^c I\to H_W(I)$ is the mapping-cocone lift whose unshifted product component is the family of ordinary limit projections and whose shifted product component is zero. This specifies the map, not merely its finite projections. Let $m_W:\mathcal R_Wq_W|_{\mathrm{good}}\xrightarrow{\sim}q^s_Wr_W^c|_{\mathrm{good}}$ be the derived reduction model fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism whose transpose under the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ is, for every good $P$, exactly $\lambda_{r_W^cP}\circ q_W((\eta^0_W)^c_P)$. Let $\rho_W:(R\lim)q^t_W\xrightarrow{\sim}q_WH_W$ be the total-limit/Roos model fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism on all complexes of strict $A_W$-module towers whose component at every K-injective tower complex $I$ is $q_W(j_I)\circ\operatorname{rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso}(\lim,I).\mathrm{hom}$. Let $a_{W,n}:B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}(-)\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{W,n}r_W$ be the finite evaluation of ordinary reduction fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism whose transpose under the quotient-extension/restriction adjunction is, for every $A_W$-module $M$, exactly $\pi_n\circ\eta^0_{W,M}:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}e_{W,n}r_WM$, where $\pi_n$ is the actual $n$th limit projection of $U_Wr_WM$ followed by its recorded evaluation/scalar-restriction identification; it is also applied termwise to complexes. For every complex $P$ of $A_Y$-modules let $B_f^0(P)$ be the strict finite pullback tower $B_f^0(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}f_n^*(B_{Y,n}\otimes_{A_Y}P)$ with its actual quotient transitions [def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower], put $T_f(P)=J_X(U_X^cF_f^cr_Y^cP)$, and let $c_{f,P}:T_f(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_f^0(P)$ be the strict tower comparison fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique strict tower isomorphism whose level-$n$ component is, in order, the complex-reordering/scalar-restriction identification, $\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(v_{f,n}^{-1})$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}f_n^*(a_{Y,n}^{-1})$. Define $F_f^{\mathrm{ref}}=\mathcal L_XD_f\mathcal R_Y$. For every good $P$, define $\mu_{f,P}:F_f^{\mathrm{ref}}(q_YP)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_XH_X(B_f^0(P))$ as the following full composite: apply $\mathcal L_XD_f$ to $m_{Y,P}$; insert the exact-derived factorization for $F_f$; insert the exact restriction/localization factorization and $\rho_X$ (this is pullbackTensorLimitRoos); and finally apply $q_XH_X$ to $c_{f,P}$. Let $\widehat f^*$ be the actual completed integral pullback and $\epsilon_{f,P}:\widehat f^*(q_YP)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_XH_X(B_f^0(P))$ its specified good-representative comparison [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-trf-integral-pullback-descent-model]. There exists a unique natural isomorphism $\alpha_f:\widehat f^*\xrightarrow{\sim}F_f^{\mathrm{ref}}$ with
$$\alpha_{f,q_YP}=\mu_{f,P}^{-1}\circ\epsilon_{f,P}\qquad\text{for every good }P.$$
This is pullbackTensorIntegralPullbackModel_existsUnique, with its full strict Roos normalization and uniqueness, on the ambient unbounded derived category.

proof.text:
For a chain map $h:P\to Q$, naturality of $a_{Y,n}^{-1}$, of $v_{f,n}^{-1}$, and of reordering/scalar restriction gives
$$c_{f,Q,n}\circ T_f(h)_n=B_f^0(h)_n\circ c_{f,P,n}.$$
Here the maps $c_{f,P}$ are already strict tower isomorphisms with exactly these components, as fixed in the core; this step does not infer transition compatibility from a derived-level comparison. Tower morphisms are componentwise families, so the displayed equalities give $c_{f,Q}\circ T_f(h)=B_f^0(h)\circ c_{f,P}$. Thus the prescribed $c_{f,P}$ form a natural isomorphism of strict-tower-valued functors. The target functor on chain maps is exactly the finite reduction, pullback and restriction functor of [def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower].

source.place: Agent assembly of the fixed core comparisons; finite-reduction compatibility supporting the sentence on finite reduction and scalar extension.

proof.text:
Restrict to good complexes. Whisker the fixed natural reduction isomorphism $m_Y$ by $\mathcal L_XD_f$, insert the natural exact-derived factorizations for $F_f$ and $U_X$, and then the fixed natural Roos isomorphism $\rho_X$. Apply $q_XH_X$ to the natural strict tower isomorphism of step 1. Their composite is a natural isomorphism
$$\mu_f:q_Y|_{\mathrm{good}}\mathbin{;}F_f^{\mathrm{ref}}\xrightarrow{\sim}(q_XH_XB_f^0)|_{\mathrm{good}}.$$
Evaluating this composite at $P$ gives, in exactly this order, the defining full composite $\mu_{f,P}$. In particular $H_X(c_{f,P})$ acts on both cone coordinates by $\prod_n c_{f,P,n}$, as in the strict Roos definition. The fixed $m_Y$ and $\rho_X$, including their adjunction-unit and K-injective augmentation normalizations, are used unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), with the fixed normalized core data; exact-derived factorization is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-integral-pullback-descent-components] with representative category the good complexes, $L=q_Y|_{\mathrm{good}}$, $F=\widehat f^*$, $T=(q_XH_XB_f^0)|_{\mathrm{good}}$, $e=\epsilon_f$, $G=F_f^{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $c=\mu_f$ from step 2. Its universal-property hypothesis is precisely the normalized pullback descent of [def-trf-integral-pullback-descent-model]. It gives a unique natural isomorphism $\alpha_f:F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ whose component is $\epsilon_{f,P}$ followed by $\mu_{f,P}^{-1}$, that is, $\mu_{f,P}^{-1}\circ\epsilon_{f,P}$. This is the required equation for every good $P$. Uniqueness is the uniqueness in that cited lemma for this same equation on all representatives; it requires neither completeness of inputs nor a claim that finite projections detect derived maps.

step.text: pullbackTensorIntegralPullbackModel_existsUnique: first prove naturality of the already prescribed strict pullback tower in the input complex. Evaluate at each finite level and use the component equations supplied by pullbackTensorPullbackTower_existsUnique. At that level, compose the natural complex-reordering comparison, the inverse-image evaluation comparison, and the reduction evaluation comparison; their composite is exactly pullbackTensorPullbackTowerLevel. Whisker the resulting natural tower isomorphism with the strict Roos functor and localization. Compose with the natural coherent reduction model, the exact inverse-image derived factorization, and the total-limit/Roos model. This proves naturality of the prescribed pullbackTensorReferencePullbackModel components. Package the composite as a natural isomorphism and prove its component formula once. Apply normalizedDescentComponents_existsUnique, the separately proved component form of integralPullbackDescent.universal. Its compatibility equation gives the required component formula by cancellation of the model isomorphism; conversely the component formula gives the universal compatibility equation by natural-transformation extensionality. The uniqueness field then proves uniqueness. These are proved private naturality/comparison helpers and a complete proof from the existing reduction, tower and Roos declarations; no new hole or changed statement is introduced.
